newsitem.title: INDIA: Relatives appeal for news of Kashmir hostages.
newsitem.headline: Relatives appeal for news of Kashmir hostages.

text.p: The families of two Britons kidnapped nearly two years ago in Kashmir distributed leaflets on Monday in the Himalayan region appealing for help in finding their loved ones.

"Have you seen these people or do you know something about them? If you have any information, please pass it to any journalist or a reliable man," the pamphlets, which carried a photograph of the hostages, said in Urdu.
Britons Paul Wells and Keith Mangan were abducted by the shadowy Al-Faran guerrilla group while trekking through the Himalayas in July 1995.
German Dirk Hasert, Norwegian Hans Christian Ostroe and Americans Donald Hutchings and John Childs were also captured.
Childs escaped and Ostroe was beheaded. There has been no trace of the other four for several months, raising doubts over whether they are still alive.

Wells' girlfriend, his father, Mangan's wife, Julie, and a cousin of hers who is heading a campaign in Britain to free the hostages circulated the pamphlets in Srinagar, summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir.
They also met senior state government officials and Kashmiri separatist leaders, who have appealed to the abductors for the hostages' release.
"We just want to know whether our dear ones are dead or alive," Julie Mangan told journalists.

The four Britons on Sunday distributed the pamphlets in the Kishtwar region, where the hostages were reported to have been sighted early last year. Kishtwar is 270 km (160 miles) southeast of Srinagar, across the Pir Panjal mountains.
The photograph of the five Western tourists printed on the leaflets was taken within a month of their kidnapping, before Ostroe was killed.
"Remember, whoever will help us in this hour of misfortune, God will help him," the appeal said.
